messages:
maria: Hey — I hit a pretty bad repro with the python async client retries. We had a POST that created a charge; server returned a 500, client retried and ended up creating the charge twice. Not ideal for non-idempotent endpoints.

alex: Oof. Do you have a minimal snippet? Are you using the built-in retry or a custom session/backoff?

maria: Using Redwood Python SDK async client default retry. No custom session. Code is basically:```py
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=KEY) as c:
    resp = await c.post('/v1/charges', json={"amount":100})
    return await resp.json()
```
Logs show first request 500, then instant retry that succeeds.

ben: Can you paste the raw HTTP logs from the SDK? Curious if the client is replaying the body correctly (streams vs buffered).

maria: Pasted below. The SDK prints: ``REQUEST 1 POST /v1/charges content-length=123`` then ``500 INTERNAL`` then immediately ``REQUEST 2 POST /v1/charges content-length=123`` and ``200 OK``. No body-changing headers.

alex: Hmm. Two hypotheses: 1) The retry policy treats 5xx as safe to retry by default (we do), but we should only auto-retry for idempotent methods like GET/PUT with an Idempotency-Key check. 2) For async streaming/body types we might be re-sending a streamed body that was already consumed, but here body is small JSON so it's not that.

ci-bot: New issue created: DEVEX-4821 "async client retries non-idempotent POST on 5xx" assigned to @alex.

alex: I'll take it. Quick notes: our current RetryPolicy maps 5xx -> retryable for all methods unless the user sets idempotency_key or marks operation non-retriable. That's too permissive.

samir: We also have a related problem where the backoff multiplier isn't applied for streaming responses — so some retries are nearly instant (0.1s), which increases chance of duplicate side-effects. Not good for billing endpoints.

alex: Good call. Repro plan: 1) Add a test that POST without idempotency-key + server 500 should NOT be retried by default. 2) Allow customers to opt-in with Idempotency-Key or explicit retry_policy. 3) Fix async streaming path to buffer small bodies or error if body is not replayable.

luis: For backwards compatibility, maybe we can flip behavior only for async client and release a patch note? Some users rely on retries for transient 5xx for POSTs.

ben: I think safe default is no auto-retry for POST/DELETE unless idempotency-key set. GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/PUT/PATCH behavior TBD (PUT can be idempotent often).

maria: Working workaround for anyone hit by this now: set client.retry_policy = RetryPolicy(max_retries=0) or add an Idempotency-Key header on your POSTs. That stopped duplicates in our system.

alex: I'll push a small change: treat non-idempotent methods as non-retriable unless idempotency-key present. Also adding explicit check and warning log when a retry is suppressed for non-idempotent method. Planning to ship a patch to 0.12.x.

samir: Can you include unit tests for both sync and async clients? Make sure streaming body tests verify we don't attempt to re-read an exhausted stream.

alex: Yep. Opening PR now, linking DEVEX-4821. Will add release note and migration doc recommending idempotency keys for mutating requests.

maria: Thanks — saved us from a weird billing mismatch with a customer.

ci-bot: PR opened: #1287 by alex -> devex/retry-fix (CI queued).

ben: Small follow-up: let's add a helper util in SDK to generate Idempotency-Key and set it automatically for high-risk endpoints unless user overrides. Could reduce friction.

alex: Good idea. I'll prototype the helper behind a feature flag.

maria: If you tag me on the PR I can test against our staging.

alex: Will do.

ci-bot: CI passed for commit 9f2a... on branch devex/retry-fix. Canaried to dev environment.

maria: Confirming staging shows single charge after canary. :tada:

luis: We'll want a short blog post or changelog entry explaining why we changed default because some users may rely on previous behavior.

alex: Agreed — adding to release notes. Closing thread when PR merges.
